lead.hed: USNI: Marines rehearse moving an air-defense radar in the Philippines
lead.insight: USNI, Thursday from Manila: the Marine Corps is forward-deploying an expeditionary air-defense radar in the Philippines as Manila modernizes coastal defense. A Marine Corps release says Marine Rotational Force – Southeast Asia tested the mobility of an AN/TPS-80 Ground/Air Task-Oriented Radar on Aug. 17. The set is a medium-range, 360-degree radar. 1st Lt. Arturo Perez, the air command-and-control officer in charge, said the work is about taking slack out of setup so U.S. and Philippine forces can share airspace. The Corps did not publish a permanent site.

political.hed: Defense News: Pentagon NATO review will give Hegseth troop options by Nov. 6
political.insight: Defense News, Thursday, citing a Pentagon Terms of Reference seen by Reuters: a review of U.S. troop deployments in Europe will produce at least four sets of options for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth by Nov. 6, ahead of a December completion date. About 80,000 U.S. forces are in Europe. The top U.S. general in Europe is to brief Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby by Sept. 18. Allied questionnaire answers are due Friday. The document does not name a cut.

political.hed: USNI: Marines publish Ground Combat Element 2040
political.insight: The Marine Corps released Ground Combat Element 2040 on Wednesday; USNI posted the document Thursday. Lt. Gen. Jay Bargeron told reporters the plan keeps conventional infantry at the center even as littoral regiments get the headlines. It adds a fifth infantry company for reconnaissance and fires, converts anti-armor gunners toward a precision-strike job with loitering munitions, and puts more mortars and a heavy-machine-gun platoon in the battalion. Bargeron said squad Marines should be able to find and strike targets out to about 20 kilometers. The 23-page paper does not change the MOS title.

political.hed: Defense News: Japan orders mass production of 3D-printed interceptor drones
political.insight: Defense News, Thursday from Manila: Japan’s Acquisition, Technology and Logistics Agency signed a mass-production deal for Terra B1, a rocket-launched interceptor drone, after a Maritime Self-Defense Force demonstration last month. ATLA did not publish the unit count or the price. The May tender sought drones that can stop one-way attack drones such as Shahed-type aircraft. CEO Toru Tokushige said 3D printing shortens prototyping and lets the company spread production so one strike does not halt the line. Tokyo wants a large unmanned fleet by 2027.

tech.hed: Marines begin fielding Squad Aiming Lasers at School of Infantry-East
tech.insight: Headquarters Marine Corps, from Camp Lejeune: Program Manager Ground Weapons Systems began fielding the Squad Aiming Laser to School of Infantry-East on July 27–28. Harry Mandeles, the optics project officer, called the near-infrared beam a generational leap from the PEQ-16, with less eye strain through night-vision goggles. The set is about three ounces lighter and nearly a half-inch shorter, mounted on the M27. Defense News notes a February 2025 award to Envision Technology worth $249 million through 2030. The Corps did not publish a fleet-wide fielding date.

tech.hed: Salesforce and Anthropic announce Claudeforce, a CRM plugin inside Claude
tech.insight: Salesforce, in a Wednesday vendor press release: the company and Anthropic launched Claudeforce, starting with Salesforce in Claude — a plugin with 37 prebuilt sales skills for pipeline updates and governed actions inside Claude. The firms say it is in a limited pilot now and expect an open beta in September 2026. Claude is also to sit inside Agentforce and become the default model for Slackbot. This is a company announcement, not an independent earnings print. Nvidia’s quarter stays with Carnegie.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty: Fellowes treats the Gilded Age as gold, not only glitter
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Thursday: John O. McGinnis reads Julian Fellowes’s HBO series The Gilded Age against Mark Twain’s insult. The essay says the show’s railroad builder, the founding of the Metropolitan Opera, and a footman’s patented alarm clock argue that new fortunes unsettled old New York and still left public goods — cheaper transport, more seats, a working patent system. McGinnis contrasts that with Succession’s zero-sum heirs. It is a reading of a drama, not a claim that the 1870s had no graft.

watch.hed: WATCH: Roosevelt families still told to plan on more than seven months
watch.insight: USNI, Wednesday from Naval Support Activity Hampton Roads: families of sailors on the Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group are preparing for a deployment lasting more than seven months as the Iran conflict continues. USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) and its escorts are in that group. The Navy did not publish a sail date. Morning lead; evening board keeps the fact on Watch.
